name: When someone runs it
description: Start the flow on demand. Says "a person starts this" out loud, which a flow with no trigger at all cannot.

name: When an object changes
description: Start the flow when one kind of object is created, updated or deleted. One event, one register, one schema — use a mapping node to normalise other shapes.

empty.message: An object trigger must name an "event" — one of: object.created, object.updated, object.deleted, object.transitioned

next-null.message: An object trigger must name an "event" — one of: object.created, object.updated, object.deleted, object.transitioned

next-good.message: An object trigger must name an "event" — one of: object.created, object.updated, object.deleted, object.transitioned

next-bad.message: An object trigger must name an "event" — one of: object.created, object.updated, object.deleted, object.transitioned

event-unknown.message: Unknown trigger event "object.moved". The engine fires: object.created, object.updated, object.deleted, object.transitioned.

no-register.message: An object trigger must name one "register". A trigger with no register either matches nothing and never fires, or matches everything — and both are silent.

no-schema.message: An object trigger must name one "schema". A trigger with no schema either matches nothing and never fires, or matches everything — and both are silent.

bad-scope.message: An object trigger scope names one "property" and one scalar "value", for example {"property": "caseType", "value": "<uuid>"}.

cron-short.message: An object trigger must name an "event" — one of: object.created, object.updated, object.deleted, object.transitioned

cron-no-runas.message: An object trigger must name an "event" — one of: object.created, object.updated, object.deleted, object.transitioned

cron-unknown-user.message: An object trigger must name an "event" — one of: object.created, object.updated, object.deleted, object.transitioned

cron-good.message: An object trigger must name an "event" — one of: object.created, object.updated, object.deleted, object.transitioned

name: On a schedule
description: Start the flow on a cron schedule. The run begins with no object — the first node has to fetch what it works on.

empty.message: A schedule trigger must carry a "cron" expression — without one nothing ever starts it, which is indistinguishable from a flow with nothing to do.

next-null.message: A schedule trigger must carry a "cron" expression — without one nothing ever starts it, which is indistinguishable from a flow with nothing to do.

next-good.message: A schedule trigger must carry a "cron" expression — without one nothing ever starts it, which is indistinguishable from a flow with nothing to do.

next-bad.message: A schedule trigger must carry a "cron" expression — without one nothing ever starts it, which is indistinguishable from a flow with nothing to do.

event-unknown.message: A schedule trigger must carry a "cron" expression — without one nothing ever starts it, which is indistinguishable from a flow with nothing to do.

no-register.message: A schedule trigger must carry a "cron" expression — without one nothing ever starts it, which is indistinguishable from a flow with nothing to do.

no-schema.message: A schedule trigger must carry a "cron" expression — without one nothing ever starts it, which is indistinguishable from a flow with nothing to do.

good-object.message: A schedule trigger must carry a "cron" expression — without one nothing ever starts it, which is indistinguishable from a flow with nothing to do.

bad-scope.message: A schedule trigger must carry a "cron" expression — without one nothing ever starts it, which is indistinguishable from a flow with nothing to do.

good-scope.message: A schedule trigger must carry a "cron" expression — without one nothing ever starts it, which is indistinguishable from a flow with nothing to do.

cron-short.message: A cron expression has five space-separated fields (minute hour day month weekday); "* * *" has 3.

cron-no-runas.message: A schedule trigger must carry a "runAs" naming the user its runs act as. Nobody is present when a schedule fires, so there is no session to take an identity from, and the flow's owner is not used as a fallback — authoring a flow is not consent to unattended execution as its author.

cron-unknown-user.message: The schedule trigger's "runAs" names "mallory", which is not an existing user account. A run that cannot resolve its acting identity is refused rather than started.
